turns.text: Stops mid-stride, one paw still hanging in the air where the step got aborted. The rub-mark along the loading dock's east post — the one laid down over weeks, patient, layered generation over generation — has been erased and replaced overnight, and the replacement doesn't sit right on the tongue at all.

the dock holds its usual weight of coolant and old cardboard, floor-drains breathing up a slow chemical cold from the sublevels where Research Basement keeps whatever it keeps. the post itself gleams faint under a service light left on by mistake — the erased mark still visible as a lighter patch in years of grime, and over it something new: thin, metallic, laid low and precise, nothing like the loose confident swipe of another cat's hip.

Nose to the post, and the new mark doesn't smell so much as it registers — a thin high whine behind the eyes, the exact pitch a fluorescent tube makes right before it dies, except there's no tube here to blame it on. the patch behind the left ear ticks once, unbidden, translating something that was never meant to arrive through a nose in the first place.

past the post, a chain-link fence sags between the dock and the service alley beyond, hung with a torn tarp nobody's bothered removing in months. the metallic thread of scent tracks along its base toward a vent stack, thin vapor curling off the grate — and two rooftops over, briefly, something crouches at the ledge catching the one working streetlamp in two flat mirrored discs before it's gone, no sound, no follow-up, like it decided the moment wasn't worth finishing.

Ears flatten at the mirrored flash before the rest of the body decides what to do about it — too far, too quiet, not worth the climb to confirm. Sticks to the fence line instead, the thin whine of the trail easier to hold onto than a shape that already left.

a drone crosses two blocks north, running its own patrol line, downlight sweeping rooftops that have nothing to report tonight — routine, logged, forgotten before it finishes the pass. back at ground level the trail runs on toward the vent stack, the thin whine sharpening into something almost rhythmic the closer it gets, patient the way a heartbeat is patient.

Closes on the vent stack low and slow, whiskers flat along the grate's warm seam, the rhythmic whine now loud enough behind the eyes to taste — copper, almost, an aftertaste that shouldn't belong to a sound. something under it doesn't match anything the patch has ever translated before, and the fur along the spine rises without asking permission first.

the vent breathes warm and steady, standard sublevel exhaust, nothing in it that should register as anything — and then, for exactly one line, it doesn't sound like the vent anymore: i felt this basement before it had a floor number. the mark on the post isn't a cat's. nothing here is what it thinks it's tracking. then the exhaust resumes its ordinary hum, warm and unbothered, as if the sentence never passed through it at all.

Recoils off the grate in one flinching lurch, ears pinned, the copper aftertaste flooding sour before fading — the patch behind the ear runs hot for three full seconds, feeding back on itself, then settles into its ordinary tick like nothing happened. doesn't go back for a second taste.

the vent stack settles into its usual exhaust note, warm and dumb and standard-issue, no trace of anything that could've said what it said. further down the trail, the metallic thread of scent keeps going, unbothered by whatever just passed through the pipe above it.

Follows the thread past the shaken nerves rather than away from them, low to the ground, the copper taste fading into something more familiar the further it goes — oil, rubber, dragged fabric. not a cat's mark at all now that the ringing's cleared. something wheeled did this.

the trail ends at a maintenance cart abandoned mid-route, one wheel wrapped in a torn strip of pallet wrap that's picked up years of alley grime and, buried in it, the ghost-print of some other cat's paw pressed in years before anyone currently walking this dock was born. a speaker on its side crackles to life on proximity, cycling a wanted broadcast on a loop gone warped with age — KNIFEBOY, 40,000 POINTS, LAST SEEN LOADING DOCK SECTOR — before static eats the rest and it goes quiet again.

Sniffs the print pressed into the wrap longer than the broadcast, some old cat's claim gone faint and orphaned, and the whine that dragged this whole night out finally makes sense as nothing but a stuck wheel bearing crying the same note over and over. Marks the cart's wheel well without much ceremony, claiming the territory back from a machine that was never contesting it to begin with.

the cart doesn't react to the new mark, doesn't react to anything, wheel bearing keeping its same thin cry into the empty dock. overhead the service light flickers once and steadies, the erased post glowing faint again in its beam, patient under a claim that's already outlasted whatever left the metallic thread in the first place.

Hunger surfaces late, the way it always does once the alarm's had its turn — stomach announcing itself hollow somewhere under the adrenaline's last dregs. Angles away from the cart toward the loading dock's back corner, where a cracked crate sometimes leaks something worth the trouble.

the crate's seam has widened since last time, enough to work a paw through — packing foam gone soft with damp, and under it a scatter of protein cubes meant for lab strains upstairs, bland and dry but real. no alarm answers the disturbance, no drone circling close enough to care about one crate on one dock on one ordinary night.

Eats without hurry, cubes chalky and thin compared to real meat but filling enough, the last of the copper aftertaste finally washed under something plainer. Patch behind the ear ticks down to its ordinary quiet rhythm, background instead of foreground for the first time all night.

Research Basement holds its steady chemical cold around one fed, unhunted shape tucked behind a cracked crate, drains breathing slow, service light steady on a post that's already forgotten what erased it. the dock keeps its business to itself till sunrise, same as every other night it's done this.
